title: Ivory satin lapel vest with ochre draped skirt
attribution_basis: Designer and season from the photograph's Wikimedia Commons category; the BASIL SODA backdrop is visible in the photo.

analysis.image_note: Photographed at the show against a dark backdrop; the skirt hem and shoes are cropped out of frame.
analysis.title: Ivory satin lapel vest with ochre draped skirt

overall.summary: A sleeveless ivory satin vest with oversized lapels is worn open over the body and cinched with two stacked embellished belts, above a high-waisted ochre satin skirt draped into soft folds. Layered gold chains and a chain-handled clutch complete the look.
overall.silhouette: An inverted triangle on top — wide, extended shoulders and broad lapels — narrowing sharply at the belted waist, then a draped column below.
overall.proportions: The waist is marked high and hard by two belts, so the skirt takes up roughly the lower two-thirds of the visible figure. The deep V of the lapels lengthens the torso visually.
overall.styling: Tailoring codes (lapels, shoulder line) are applied to a sleeveless top and paired with an eveningwear satin skirt. Jewellery is layered heavily at the neckline to fill the open V.
overall.aesthetic: Sharp-shouldered, glamorous daywear-to-evening with a 1980s power-shoulder reference softened by fluid satin.

combinations: Ivory and ochre: a light/dark split at the waist
Gold metal repeated from neck to waist to hand
colors.interaction: The ochre of the skirt reappears in the collar facing, linking top and bottom. Black belts create a hard horizontal break between the two main colours, and the gold jewellery bridges them.

garments.name: Sleeveless satin vest with oversized lapels
garments.silhouette_fit: Structured, with extended shoulders that project past the natural shoulder point; open to the waist.

fabric.description: High-sheen satin with some body, holding the lapel shape.

garments.uncertainty: It is not visible whether the vest closes or is worn fully open beneath the belts.

garments.name: High-waisted draped satin skirt
garments.silhouette_fit: Fitted at the waist, then gathered into diagonal drapes over the hips; narrow overall.
details: Soft gathered drape at the front
garments.uncertainty: The hem and length are cropped out of the photo.

garments.name: Two stacked embellished waist belts
garments.silhouette_fit: Worn tight at the natural waist.

fabric.description: Appears to be leather or a leather-like band with metal hardware.

garments.name: Layered gold chain necklaces
garments.silhouette_fit: Long, falling into the neckline V.

design_details.detail: The shoulder line extends well beyond the body and is cut squarely, creating width without sleeves.
Very wide lapels run down to the waist, forming a deep V that frames the jewellery.
An ochre facing shows at the back of the collar, repeating the skirt colour.
Two belts are stacked to make a deep waistband, a strong horizontal against the vertical lapels.
Fabric is gathered diagonally, likely from tucks or pleats at the waist seam.

vocabulary.definition: The folded-back front edge of a jacket or coat that continues from the collar.
vocabulary.application: Here the lapels are unusually wide and long, carried onto a sleeveless vest.
vocabulary.contrast: A notch lapel has a V-shaped cut where it meets the collar; a shawl lapel is one continuous curve with no notch.

vocabulary.definition: A shoulder line that sits beyond the wearer's natural shoulder point.
vocabulary.application: The vest's squared shoulders project outward, widening the upper body.
vocabulary.contrast: A dropped shoulder falls down the arm and looks relaxed; an extended shoulder stays high and looks structured.

vocabulary.definition: How fabric hangs and folds under its own weight, or folds deliberately arranged by the designer.
vocabulary.application: The satin skirt is draped into diagonal folds across the front.
vocabulary.contrast: Pleats are folds pressed or stitched in place; drape folds are softer and move.

vocabulary.definition: A waist pulled in tightly, usually by a belt or corsetry, to emphasise it.
vocabulary.application: Two belts mark and narrow the waist between the wide top and the skirt.

vocabulary.definition: A shape that is widest at the shoulders and narrows downward.
vocabulary.application: Broad shoulders and lapels taper to the belted waist.
vocabulary.contrast: An A-line silhouette does the opposite: narrow at the top and widening toward the hem.

vocabulary.definition: A weave with long floating threads on the surface, giving a smooth, shiny face.
vocabulary.application: Both the vest and skirt show the high sheen typical of satin.
vocabulary.contrast: Matte crepe has a dry, grainy surface and diffuses light instead of reflecting it.

possible_brands.name: Basil Soda
possible_brands.reasoning: The designer's name is printed on the backdrop.

title: Stand-collar ivory vest over a tulle skirt
attribution_basis: Designer and season from the photograph's Wikimedia Commons category.

analysis.image_note: Backstage photograph with low light; the lower skirt is in shadow.
analysis.title: Stand-collar ivory vest over a tulle skirt

overall.summary: A long, sleeveless ivory satin vest with a high stand collar and flap pocket is belted with stacked gold-studded belts over a full, translucent taupe tulle skirt.
overall.silhouette: A narrow, structured upper body over a voluminous, airy skirt.
overall.proportions: The vest runs past the hip, so the belts sit in the middle of the garment; the tulle skirt spreads out beneath it.
overall.styling: Hard tailoring is contrasted with soft, sheer volume — a day-jacket idea worn over an evening skirt.

colors.interaction: The pale vest reads as a solid block against the dark, see-through skirt, and the black-and-gold belts sharpen the meeting point.

garments.name: Longline sleeveless vest with stand collar
garments.silhouette_fit: Fitted through the body, hip length or longer, with squared shoulders.
details: Front zip or placket with dark trim
garments.uncertainty: The exact closure (zip or concealed placket) is unclear.

garments.name: Full tulle skirt
garments.silhouette_fit: Voluminous, flaring from beneath the vest.
garments.uncertainty: Length and waist are hidden by the vest and shadows.

design_details.detail: A stand collar rises straight up the neck with no fold-over, giving a uniform-like edge.
A flap pocket sits low on the hip, a menswear detail.
Volume is built from several layers of sheer fabric rather than one stiff layer.

vocabulary.definition: A collar that stands up around the neck without folding over.
vocabulary.application: The vest's collar rises straight up, adding height and formality.
vocabulary.contrast: A shirt collar folds down over a collar stand; a stand collar is only the upright band.

vocabulary.definition: A pocket covered by a separate piece of fabric (the flap).
vocabulary.application: A flap pocket at the hip borrows from tailored jackets.
vocabulary.contrast: A patch pocket is sewn onto the outside with no flap; a welt pocket is a slit finished with a narrow strip.

vocabulary.definition: A lightweight, fine net fabric often used in layers for volume.
vocabulary.application: The skirt's sheer, smoky layers create volume without weight.
vocabulary.contrast: Organza is also sheer but is a woven fabric with a crisper, smoother surface.

vocabulary.definition: Describes a top or jacket cut longer than usual.
vocabulary.application: The vest extends past the hip.
vocabulary.contrast: A cropped jacket ends above the waist.

title: Grey halter gown with interlaced pintucked straps
attribution_basis: Designer and season from the photograph's Wikimedia Commons category.

analysis.image_note: Backstage photograph cropped at the hip; the skirt is not visible.
analysis.title: Grey halter gown with interlaced pintucked straps

overall.summary: A dove-grey gown whose bodice is formed by two bands of fine pintucked fabric that cross at the throat as a halter and interlace down the centre front before releasing into soft drapes at the waist.
overall.silhouette: Close-fitting bodice with bare shoulders; the visible part suggests a column or softly draped gown.
overall.proportions: The interlaced bands create a strong vertical line down the centre, lengthening the torso.
overall.styling: Minimal styling — hair pulled back, no visible jewellery — so the construction is the focus.
overall.aesthetic: Grecian-inspired couture drapery with a precise, technical surface.

colors.interaction: A single colour lets light and shadow on the tucks and drapes do the work instead of contrast.

garments.name: Halter-neck gown with interlaced bodice
garments.silhouette_fit: Fitted through the bodice, releasing into drape at the waist.
details: Bands of narrow pintucks interlaced at centre front

fabric.description: Matte, fluid fabric such as silk crepe or jersey.

garments.uncertainty: The skirt and back are not visible.

design_details.detail: Two bands cross at the throat and wrap behind the neck, leaving the shoulders bare.
The bands twist around each other in an interlaced pattern down the bodice.
Each band is covered in narrow parallel tucks, adding texture and some rigidity.
Below the bodice the fabric falls into soft, unpressed folds.

vocabulary.definition: A neckline held up by a strap or band that goes around the back of the neck.
vocabulary.application: The crossed bands form the halter and leave the shoulders and arms bare.
vocabulary.contrast: A strapless bodice has no support over the shoulders or neck at all.

vocabulary.definition: Very narrow stitched folds, usually in parallel rows, used for texture or shaping.
vocabulary.application: The interlaced bands are made of rows of fine pintucks.
vocabulary.contrast: Pleats are wider folds and are usually left free at one end; pintucks are stitched along their length.

vocabulary.definition: How fabric falls and folds, often arranged by hand on a dress form.
vocabulary.application: The fabric relaxes into drapes below the structured bodice.

title: Cerulean draped gown with embellished bodice
attribution_basis: Designer and season from the photograph's Wikimedia Commons category.

analysis.image_note: Backstage photograph; the lower skirt is out of frame.
analysis.title: Cerulean draped gown with embellished bodice

overall.summary: A bright cerulean gown with a sweetheart-shaped panel of silver embroidery at the bust, embellished shoulders, and heavy cowl drapes falling from the bust across the midriff.
overall.silhouette: Fluid and body-skimming, with volume concentrated in the drapes at the front.
overall.proportions: The embellishment is placed high on the body, drawing the eye to the shoulders and bust.
overall.styling: Sleek, lifted hair and strong blue eye make-up echo the gown's colour.
overall.aesthetic: Couture evening glamour with Grecian drapery and jewel-like embroidery.

colors.interaction: The silver embroidery picks up light and contrasts with the saturated blue, while shadows in the drapes give the colour depth.

garments.name: Draped evening gown with embroidered bust panel
garments.silhouette_fit: Body-skimming with soft cowl drapes across the front.

fabric.description: A fluid, lightly lustrous fabric such as silk chiffon or charmeuse.

garments.uncertainty: Skirt length and back construction are not visible.

design_details.detail: Silver beading forms a curved, sweetheart-like panel.
The wide straps are also embellished, framing the neckline.
Fabric hangs in loose U-shaped folds below the bust, typical of a cowl.
The drapes are likely cut on the bias so they fall softly.

vocabulary.definition: Fabric that falls in soft, rounded U-shaped folds, often at the neck or front.
vocabulary.application: Loose folds hang from beneath the embroidered bust.
vocabulary.contrast: Ruching gathers fabric tightly into small puckers; a cowl hangs loosely.

vocabulary.definition: Decoration added to fabric, such as beads, sequins or embroidery.
vocabulary.application: Silver beadwork covers the bust panel and straps.

vocabulary.definition: Cutting fabric at 45° to the grain so it stretches and drapes more fluidly.
vocabulary.application: The soft fall of the drapes suggests bias-cut fabric (an inference).
vocabulary.contrast: Straight-grain cutting is more stable and hangs straighter.

title: Emerald chiffon gown with embroidered V-neck bodice
attribution_basis: Designer and season from the photograph's Wikimedia Commons category.

analysis.image_note: Backstage photograph with motion in the skirt.
analysis.title: Emerald chiffon gown with embroidered V-neck bodice

overall.summary: An emerald gown with a deep V neckline, short embroidered cap sleeves and a fitted embellished bodice, opening into a long, floating chiffon skirt.
overall.silhouette: Fitted bodice and defined waist over a full, flowing floor-length skirt.
overall.proportions: The embellishment stops at a marked waist, giving a clear split between the decorated bodice and the plain, airy skirt.
overall.styling: Hair is swept up into a sculpted chignon, keeping the shoulders and neckline clear.

colors.interaction: Sheer layers make the skirt look lighter than the dense, embroidered bodice even though the colour is the same.

garments.name: V-neck evening gown with embroidered bodice and chiffon skirt
garments.silhouette_fit: Fitted bodice with a gathered, floor-length skirt.

fabric.description: Sheer, lightweight chiffon in the skirt.

design_details.detail: A deep V plunges toward the waist and is edged in embroidery.
Short cap sleeves just cover the shoulder and carry the same embroidery.
Several layers of sheer fabric are gathered into the waist and move freely.

vocabulary.definition: A very short sleeve that covers only the top of the shoulder.
vocabulary.application: The embroidered sleeves sit just over the shoulder.
vocabulary.contrast: A short sleeve continues down the upper arm; a cap sleeve stops at the shoulder.

vocabulary.definition: A sheer, lightweight plain-weave fabric with a soft drape.
vocabulary.contrast: Georgette is similar but slightly heavier with a crinkled surface.

vocabulary.definition: A silhouette that is fitted through the bodice and flares out below the waist.
vocabulary.application: The fitted embroidered bodice gives way to a wide, flowing skirt.
vocabulary.contrast: A sheath or column stays close to the body all the way down.
